what_it_buys: An address collision that a channel selection can resolve, and the register whose readback is the whole question.
what_it_does_not_buy: Nothing about any sensor, and nothing electrical about a specific wiring.

item: Identical I2C sensors with a fixed shared address (e.g. two of one IMU part)
purpose: The collision. Two devices answering one address is why a mux is bought.
what_it_buys: The ability for a misattribution to exist at all. With distinct addresses there is nothing to confuse.
what_it_does_not_buy: Nothing about sensor accuracy; these are identity tokens, not instruments.

item: One I2C sensor at a distinct address
what_it_buys: A channel whose identity no selection error can confuse, so a null result is distinguishable from a dead harness.

item: I2C host with readable bus (SBC or MCU dev board)
purpose: Issues selections and readbacks; runs the acquisition code.
what_it_buys: The host-side record that is the object under test.
what_it_does_not_buy: No timing claim that transfers to flight hardware or a companion computer.
reuse_existing: YES -- check whether the E2 Linux host suffices

item: Logic analyser or oscilloscope, >= 2 channels, I2C decode
purpose: The INDEPENDENT record of what was actually on the wire.
what_it_buys: Adjudication by something other than the system under test. Without it the campaign is self-certifying (see IV-1).
what_it_does_not_buy: Nothing the host can also see; its value is precisely that it is not the host.

item: Switched supply for the mux rail only
purpose: Creates the BROWNOUT condition: reset the mux without resetting the host.
what_it_buys: The POR_RESET failure mode as a physical event rather than a simulated one.
